text: why is the water rendering again when im doing a negative value
resolution: The user asked why water still renders on a negative slider value and explained the model: water only ever exists IN a basin that holds it, never above ground, so the slider is just pool DEPTH and a negative is meaningless. Root cause: water mode reused the generic terrain 'height z' slider (signed, -HEIGHT_LIMIT..HEIGHT_LIMIT); since the brush reads |centerZ| as depth, a negative value still painted a pool, which read as a bug. Fixed in 7f7fbfc25 by giving water mode a dedicated WaterSection with a single positive 'depth' slider (0.5..HEIGHT_LIMIT metres, stored in centerZ). Pure UI change — the brush already excavates+fills a flush basin, so positive-value behavior is unchanged; negatives simply can no longer be entered. Editor hot-reloads, no rebuild/bake needed for the rail.
